question.text: In the growth option of a mutual fund scheme, the gains made in the portfolio are:

answer.text: Not distributed but retained in the fund, reflected in a rising NAV
Distributed periodically to unit holders as dividends
Reinvested in purchasing additional units for the investor
Transferred to the investor's bank account every quarter

explanation.text: The Logic: In the growth option, gains made in the portfolio are not distributed but retained in the fund. The gains are reflected in the rising NAV over time, and investors realise these gains only when they sell (redeem) their units. The Trap: Distributing gains as cash is the IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) pay-out option. Reinvesting gains in additional units is the IDCW re-investment option. Under the growth option, NAV grows but nothing is separately paid out or reinvested into new units. Note: The "Dividend" terminology used historically was renamed by SEBI to "Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal (IDCW)" to make clear that pay-outs include a return of capital.
